result: MiR-146a is a critical negative regulator of inflammation that targets TRAF6 and IRAK1 upstream of NF-κB. Mice with targeted miR-146a deletion develop NF-κB-driven chronic inflammation spontaneously with aging.

result: The molecular mechanism involves a miR-146a/TRAF6/NF-κB/IL-6 axis. NF-κB is hyperactivated in miR-146a-deficient HSCs after LPS stimulation, and deleting p50 rescues HSC defects, myeloproliferative disease, and myeloid cancer in miR-146a KO mice.
